vendors.name: Claude
vendors.tagline: Flat-rate Claude Code access with opaque, relative limits.
vendors.summary: Pro and Max give access to Claude Code and the full model range through 5-hour and weekly limits. Anthropic publishes limits only as multiples of Pro, so the dollar value of each plan has to be inferred from usage data.
strengths: Top of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (Opus 5.5 at 58, Sonnet 5.5 at 56)
Flat-rate Max tiers can carry a large subsidy for heavy agentic use (our values are estimates, so check against your own usage data)
Usage credits let you overflow at standard API rates instead of being cut off
caveats: Dollar allotments are unpublished; our values are estimates with wide ranges
Weekly caps and capacity-based limits can change without notice
Fable access on Pro/Max is limited (usage credits, or 50% of weekly limits on Max)

vendors.name: ChatGPT / Codex
vendors.tagline: Codex is bundled into ChatGPT plans, with Pro now at three price points.
vendors.summary: Codex (CLI, IDE, cloud, desktop) is included in ChatGPT Free through Enterprise and shares usage with ChatGPT Work. Plus has published local-message ranges per 5 hours; Pro comes at $100, $200 and $500 with no 5-hour limit.
strengths: GPT-6.1 Sol scores 52 on the AA index at a fraction of the per-task cost of Opus 5.5 ($0.72 vs $5.98)
Clear credit rate card makes overflow pricing transparent
Cheap Luna model stretches the allowance for lightweight tasks
caveats: Dollar value of included usage is not published for any tier; our values are estimates
Fast (2.5x) and Ultrafast (8x) modes burn the included allowance much faster
GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT and Codex on 2026-10-14

vendors.name: Cursor
vendors.tagline: Included usage pools billed at API price, plus cheap first-party models.
vendors.summary: Pro ($20), Pro+ ($60) and Ultra ($200) each include a pool of third-party model usage charged at the model's API rate, and a separate bigger pool for Cursor's own models (Grok, Composer). Heavier users go on-demand at the same API rates.
strengths: Any frontier model from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and others in one editor
Transparent: third-party usage is charged at exact API list price
Cursor Models pool (Grok 4.x, Composer 2.5) adds usage on top of the dollar pool
caveats: Per-tier dollar amounts are not on the fetched pricing page; values follow Cursor's earlier published tiers
At list-price billing, subsidy on third-party models is smaller than on flat-rate plans
Teams add a $0.25/M-token Cursor Token Rate on third-party models

vendors.name: GitHub Copilot
vendors.tagline: AI Credits worth more than the sticker price, published to the dollar.
vendors.summary: Copilot moved to GitHub AI Credits (1 credit = $0.01). Every paid plan includes a base allotment equal to its price plus a flex allotment on top. Completions stay unlimited and credit-free.
strengths: The only major plan family that publishes its exact dollar allotment per tier
Subsidy ratio rises with tier: 1.5x (Pro), 1.8x (Pro+), 2.0x (Max)
Widest model menu (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, Kimi) under one bill
caveats: Flex allotment may change over time
Credits drain by model cost, so frontier models still use the allowance quickly
Not the highest multiple available versus subscription-with-limits products

vendors.name: Devin / Windsurf
vendors.tagline: Windsurf pricing now lives on the Devin page.
vendors.summary: windsurf.com/pricing resolves to Devin's pricing: Pro $20 and Max $200, each with daily and weekly refreshing quotas, overflow at API pricing, plus SWE-2 free in Devin Desktop and CLI through 2026-10-16.
strengths: Includes cloud agents (Devin Cloud) with the individual plan
Frontier models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and SpaceXAI
Free SWE-2 promo through 2026-10-16
caveats: Quota size is not published in dollars or tokens
Only two paid individual tiers ($20 and $200), with no mid-priced step

vendors.name: Kiro
vendors.tagline: Credit tiers from $20 to $200 at a flat $0.04 per credit.
vendors.summary: Kiro sells 1,000 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 credits per month at $20 / $40 / $100 / $200, with add-on credits at $0.04. At that rate each tier is worth 2x its price.
strengths: Simple, linear credit ladder with a published overflow price
Access to Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 and open-weight models
$20 sign-up credit on first upgrade
caveats: Credits are not tokens; the 2x figure is measured at Kiro's own credit price
Model menu on the pricing page lags the newest releases
Credit cost varies by model via multipliers

vendors.name: Zed
vendors.tagline: Editor first; hosted AI is pass-through plus 10%.
vendors.summary: Zed Pro is $10/mo with $5 of hosted tokens and unlimited edit predictions; beyond that, tokens are billed at API list +10%. Bring your own keys, Claude Agent or Codex CLI for free on Personal.
strengths: Bring-your-own-key and external agents are free
Honest pass-through pricing with no hidden multiple
caveats: Not a subsidy play: hosted tokens cost slightly more than API list
Value is in the editor and predictions, not bulk tokens

vendors.name: Google AI + Antigravity
vendors.tagline: Coding limits bundled inside broader Google AI plans.
vendors.summary: Antigravity has a free tier, with higher limits and a flexible AI credit pool on Google AI Pro ($19.99) and Ultra. Jules and AI Studio limits scale the same way. Plans also bundle storage, Workspace AI and more.
strengths: Free tier with unlimited tab completions
Bundled value beyond coding (storage, Cloud credits, Workspace AI)
Gemini 4 Argon scores 53 on the AA index
caveats: Coding allotment is not quantified; values here are rough estimates
A bundle: coding value is only a slice of what you pay for
Ultra price was not visible on the fetched page
